module.purpose: Manages concurrent update queueing in React's fiber reconciler: buffers updates arriving during an in-progress render and attaches them to fiber/hook/class queues after render, marking lanes from fiber to root and handling offscreen hidden boundaries.
module.summary: This module implements the concurrency-safe update queueing mechanism for React's fiber renderer. When updates arrive from concurrent events during a render, they are stashed in a module-level array and later attached to fiber/hook/class queues by finishQueueingConcurrentUpdates. It provides functions to enqueue hook updates, class updates, render lanes, and to mark update lanes from a fiber up to the root, walking the parent chain and handling offscreen hidden boundaries. It also includes dev-only detection of updates on not-yet-mounted fibers and infinite update loop protection.
module.businessContext: React reconciliation internals; ensures concurrent updates don't corrupt in-progress renders. Failure can drop updates or cause infinite loops.

detail.name: finishQueueingConcurrentUpdates
preconditions: concurrentQueues contains quadruples (fiber, queue, update, lane) for indices i < concurrentQueuesIndex
concurrentQueuesIndex is a non-negative integer representing the number of buffered entries * 4
postconditions: concurrentQueuesIndex is reset to 0
concurrentlyUpdatedLanes is reset to NoLanes
all processed slots in concurrentQueues up to endIndex are set to null
for each non-null (queue, update) pair, update is linked into queue.pending circular list
queue.pending references the newly linked update
invariants: entries are processed strictly in groups of 4 (fiber, queue, update, lane)
when queue.pending was null, the inserted update forms a self-referential circular list (update.next = update)
edgeCases: queue.pending === null: update.next = update (first update creates circular list)
queue === null or update === null: no linking occurs, but the four slots are still nulled
concurrentQueuesIndex === 0 (empty buffer): loop does not run; only resets occur
stateMutations: concurrentQueues[i] slots nulled for processed indices
update.next mutated to insert into circular list
detail.summary: Drains the buffered concurrent update queue, linking each update into its target fiber's update queue and resetting global concurrency bookkeeping (index and lane tracker).

units.name: enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout

detail.name: enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout
detail.signature: export function enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout<S, A>(fiber: Fiber, queue: HookQueue<S, A>, update: HookUpdate<S, A>): void
preconditions: fiber must be a non-null Fiber instance.
queue must be a valid HookQueue for the given generic types S and A.
update must conform to the HookUpdate<S, A> shape expected by enqueueUpdate.
postconditions: The update is enqueued into the fiber's hook queue via enqueueUpdate.
No synchronous re-render is triggered for this update.
Returns void.
invariants: The update is always retained in the queue until a rebase occurs or the fiber unmounts.
No root is returned or re-rendered eagerly.
edgeCases: If queue is null or undefined, enqueueUpdate will likely throw or silently fail depending on implementation.
If update has no payload or action, it is still enqueued but may be a no-op during rebase.
If fiber is unmounted, the update remains queued but may be discarded during lane pruning.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Behavior is undefined if fiber, queue, or update are malformed; no explicit guard is present in source.

stateMutations: Mutates the hook queue (HookQueue<S, A>) by appending the update via enqueueUpdate.
No direct mutation of fiber state occurs beyond queue linkage.
detail.summary: Queues a hook update that bypasses immediate re-rendering, storing it solely so a subsequent higher-priority update can rebase against it. Used to eagerly bail out of rendering while preserving correctness of later concurrent updates.

detail.name: detectUpdateOnUnmountedFiber
preconditions: The fiber argument must be a Fiber node or null
The fiber tree must have valid return pointers linking child to parent up to the root
postconditions: Returns true if the fiber or any ancestor is in a hidden offscreen state, false otherwise
Does not mutate the fiber tree or any external state
invariants: The isHidden flag starts false and is only ever set to true (never reset) during traversal
Each loop iteration advances parent via parent.return until reaching the root
edgeCases: If fiber is null, returns false without traversal
If the fiber has no offscreen state, isHidden remains false and false is returned
An offscreenInstance with _visibility lacking the OffscreenVisible bit sets isHidden to true
If offscreenInstance is null at any ancestor level, that level does not affect isHidden

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns false when fiber is null

detail.summary: Traverses a fiber's ancestor chain to check offscreen visibility flags, returning true when the fiber or an ancestor is hidden in an offscreen boundary, which indicates the update landed on a fiber that is effectively unmounted.

specLiterals.role: Visibility bitmask flag checked against offscreenInstance._visibility to determine if the offscreen tree is currently visible
Null sentinel used to terminate fiber-return traversal and guard offscreenInstance checks
